numberItems.stem: How many steps does the handbook list for **coupling** a tractor-semitrailer?
numberItems.explanation: The handbook lists 16 coupling steps (pp. 6-9–6-10) and 10 uncoupling steps (p. 6-11).

numberItems.stem: Which are the first three coupling steps, in order?
options: Position the tractor; back slowly; inspect the fifth wheel
Inspect the fifth wheel; inspect the area and chock the wheels; position the tractor
Chock the wheels; connect the air lines; back under the trailer
numberItems.explanation: Step 1 is inspecting the fifth wheel, Step 2 inspecting the area and chocking the wheels, Step 3 positioning the tractor (p. 6-9).

numberItems.stem: Which describes a fifth wheel that is ready for coupling?
options: Level, jaws open, safety handle in the automatic lock position
Tilted down toward the rear, jaws closed, sliding fifth wheel unlocked
Tilted down toward the rear of the tractor, jaws open, safety handle in the automatic lock position
numberItems.explanation: Ready for coupling: tilted down toward the rear of the tractor, jaws open, safety unlocking handle in the automatic lock position, and a sliding fifth wheel locked (p. 6-9).

numberItems.stem: You check the trailer height before backing under. What may happen if the trailer is too **high**?
options: The tractor may strike and damage the trailer nose
The trailer may not couple correctly
The landing gear may collapse
numberItems.explanation: If the trailer is too high it may not couple correctly; if too low, the tractor may strike and damage the trailer nose (p. 6-9).

numberItems.stem: You have checked the trailer height. What must you do before backing under the trailer?
options: Connect the air lines, supply air and check the brakes, then lock the trailer brakes
Raise the landing gear and plug in the electrical cord
Nothing more — back under first, then connect the air lines
numberItems.explanation: Steps 7–9 (connect air lines, supply air and check for crossed lines, lock the trailer brakes) come before Step 10, backing under (pp. 6-9–6-10).

numberItems.stem: During the crossed-air-line check, why do you shut the engine off?
options: So the tractor protection valve closes
To save air pressure
So you can hear the trailer brakes apply and release
numberItems.explanation: Shut the engine off so you can hear the brakes; you should hear the brakes move when applied and air escape when released (p. 6-9).

numberItems.stem: Which gear should you use to back under the trailer?
options: The highest reverse gear
The lowest reverse gear
Neutral, letting the tractor roll back
numberItems.explanation: Use the lowest reverse gear and back slowly to avoid hitting the kingpin too hard (p. 6-10).

numberItems.stem: During the tug test, how should the landing gear and trailer brakes be set?
options: Landing gear raised slightly off the ground; trailer brakes still locked
Landing gear all the way up; trailer brakes released
Landing gear firmly on the ground; trailer brakes released
numberItems.explanation: Raise the landing gear slightly off the ground and pull gently forward while the trailer brakes are still locked (p. 6-10).

numberItems.stem: After coupling, how much space should there be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
options: A small gap is normal
None
numberItems.explanation: There must be no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel; a gap may mean the kingpin is on top of the closed jaws (p. 6-10). 0.3–0.5 mm is the drawbar clearance.

numberItems.stem: You look into the back of the fifth wheel. The jaws should be closed around which part of the kingpin?
options: The head
The shank
The top plate
numberItems.explanation: Make sure the fifth-wheel jaws have closed around the shank of the kingpin (p. 6-10).

numberItems.stem: How far should the landing gear be raised before you drive?
options: Just until it lifts off the pavement
Halfway, so it can catch the trailer if needed
All the way up, with the crank handle secured
numberItems.explanation: Raise the landing gear all the way up and secure the crank handle; gear left part way up may catch on railroad tracks or other things (p. 6-10).

numberItems.stem: When uncoupling, how should you hang the trailer's electrical cable?
options: With the plug down
With the plug up
Wrapped around the glad hands
numberItems.explanation: Hang the electrical cable with the plug down to prevent moisture from entering it (p. 6-11).

numberItems.stem: [CA] When coupling a ball-type drawbar, to what torque do you tighten both safety lock screws?
options: 350 to 400 newton meters (Nm)
Just hand-tight
0.3 to 0.5 newton meters (Nm)
numberItems.explanation: Tighten both lock screws with their self-locking nuts at a 350 to 400 Nm torque wrench setting (p. 6-13). 0.3–0.5 mm is the vertical clearance setting, not a torque.

numberItems.stem: Which trailers are required by law to have safety chains?
options: Only gooseneck trailers
Only trailers without their own brakes
All trailers
numberItems.explanation: All trailers are required by law to have safety chains (p. 6-15).
